text: Hello and welcome to our LIVE commentary of the Premier League fixture between Newcastle United and Wolves!
Winless in their last two Premier League fixtures, Newcastle United welcome Wolves to St.
James’ Park in search of their first home victory of 2024.

Buoyed by their midweek penalty shoot-out victory over Blackburn in the FA Cup, Eddie Howe’s side can jump their opponents today with a victory and could finish the weekend as high as seventh if other results around the league go their way.
In-form Wolves look to extend their winning run in the league to three-consecutive games, beating both Tottenham and Sheffield United on back-to-back weekends.

Ninth in the table - a point behind Brighton in seventh - Gary O’Neil’s team are sixth in the form table since the turn of the year with only the current top three as well as Manchester United and Aston Villa amassing more points in that period.
With 15 minutes to go before kick-off, let’s take a look at how the two sides are lining up - starting with our hosts!
Newcastle make four alterations to the XI that lost 4-1 to Arsenal seven days ago.
Dubravka has returned to fitness and replaces Karius between the posts, while Burn is preferred to Livramento at right-back.
Miley is given a rest as Willock takes over in central midfield and on the right wing, Murphy is picked ahead of Almiron.

Wolves make two changes to the side that beat Sheffield United 1-0 on Sunday, as Doyle replaces the uninvolved Joao Gomes in midfield, and Bellegarde gets his eighth start of the campaign at striker, with Hwang Hee-Chan not featuring due to a hamstring injury.
Newcastle get the match underway from the kick-off!
Gordon cuts inside from the left after receiving a pass from Willock and teases a cross to the far post for Murphy, who is beaten in the air by a leaping Ait Nouri.
Neto goes on a brilliantly incisive run through the heart of Newcastle’s midfield, drawing as many as three defenders towards him as he breaks into the penalty area.
With only Dubravka to beat, the forward is unable to get the ball out from underneath his feet, allowing Schar to put in a last-ditch sliding challenge that wins possession back for the hosts.
Sarabia receives the ball on the turn just outside the penalty area before stepping past Schar and dispatching a left-footed shot that takes a deflection on its way behind for a corner.
The skies have opened up above St.
James’ Park, with sheets of rain steadily flowing down onto the pitch.
The goalkeepers will have to be assured in their handling of the ball in the conditions, while the slippery surface could lead to a more chaotic game for the outfield players.

Gordon looks for a one-two pass with Isak on the edge of the 18-yard box, but the striker’s return isn’t as accurate as it needed to be, with Semedo able to step forward and put it out for a throw-in.

Ait Nouri spots the run of Bellegarde off the shoulder of Trippier and looks to play his team-mate in behind the opposition defence but the striker is unable to hold his run, failing to control the initial pass and prompting the referee to blow his whistle for offside.
Semedo drives to the byline and chips a cross in towards the far post but Bellegarde is beaten in the air by Trippier, who temporarily clears the danger.

NEWCASTLE TAKE THE LEAD! 1-0! It’s a slightly fortuitous goal but the home supporters won’t care - with Isak giving Newcastle an early advantage! Gordon gets forward on a counter-attack after a long period of possession for Wolves, slipping the ball through for Guimaraes on the overlapping run.
The midfielder hits his shot from close range which is deflected by Dawson, right into the path of Isak, who nods it home!
Neto scampers to the byline and looks to pick Bellegarde out with a centring pass towards the penalty spot but Botman is there to whack the ball back into Wolves’ half.
It’s the first time in over three matches that Wolves find themselves behind in a Premier League fixture - since a 2-0 loss to Brentford on February 2.
O’Neil’s side will have to show determination and character to pull themselves back level away from home - without the injured Hwang - who has 10 goals this year.
Gordon takes up a position wide on the left flank, giving Burn space to run into through the middle of the park.
The winger picks out his team-mate with an incisive pass, allowing the full-back to take a touch to set himself before dragging his shot well wide of the far post from 20 yards out.
JUST OVER! Sarabia’s inswinging corner finds the head of Dawson, who prods the ball on to Bellegarde.
Knowing nothing of the delivery, the forward gets a touch to the flick-on, doing just enough to put it into Mario Lemina’s path.
Rising higher than his marker, the midfielder makes great contact with the ball but puts his chance just high of the crossbar!
Bellegarde’s foul on Guimaraes gives Newcastle a free-kick in a dangerous, central position 25 yards from goal.
Trippier is tasked with taking the set-piece but he sends his strike directly into the wall, which does its job and puts the ball for a throw.

Toti launches a pass deep into Newcastle’s half for Neto but the diminutive forward is always less likely to win an aerial duel against the imposing Burn, who wins the battle and puts it out of play to give the rest of his team time to retreat.
Neto plays a corner short to Sarabia, whose delivery towards the penalty spot from a deep position on the right wing is easily beaten away by Longstaff.
Murphy cuts inside from the left and curls a tame shot towards goal that’s easily caught by Sa.
Dawson plays a risky pass through the middle of the pitch from inside his own penalty area but Neto is upended by Willock, giving Wolves a chance to regroup at a position higher up the field.
NEWCASTLE STRIKE AGAIN! 2-0! Murphy gets free down the right wing and shapes his body to curl a low cross in towards the penalty spot for Isak.

Sa comes rushing off his line to beat the forward to the delivery but a collision leaves the ball unclaimed just outside the six-yard box, with Gordon coming across to tap his finish into the empty net to double the advantage!

events.action: tap his finish into the empty net

text: Trippier and Gordon work a short-corner routine that gets Murphy into a pocket of space 30 yards from goal but the winger’s strike from distance flies harmlessly over Sa’s crossbar.

The 17 previous Premier League meetings between Newcastle and Wolves have seen both sides score 16 times, with the only clean sheet in this fixture in the competition coming via the Magpies’ 1-0 win in April 2022.
The ball is popped over the top of the defence for Neto, who steps towards the byline before chipping the ball across the face of goal to the far post for Bellegarde.
The forward gets in behind Burn and makes contact with his header but he sends it up and over the crossbar before an offside call in the build-up gives Newcastle a chance to clear their lines.

Neto looks to cut inside and dispatch a shot but the Newcastle defence is well aware of the forward’s intentions, with both Burn and Botman combining to close down the space before forcing an errant pass across the pitch for Doyle, which is intercepted by Murphy.
Semedo gets the better of Gordon this time, squeezing himself between the player and the ball before winning a free-kick right beside his own corner-flag.
The fourth official indicates three minutes will be added to the end of the half for stoppages.
Neto looks to be limping significantly after an aerial duel with Schar, in which the defender unwittingly ran his studs down the leg of the winger.
It’s a painful one, but down two goals, his coach will be hoping he’ll be able to continue.
HALF-TIME: NEWCASTLE UNITED 2-0 WOLVES.
A wet and windy first half at St.
James’ Park comes to a close with Newcastle ahead by two goals to nil, thanks to opportunistic finishes from Isak and Gordon 19 minutes apart.

Wolves started the match with intent, with Sarabia and Neto looking to pull the strings for the visitors, but the resolute pairing of Schar and Botman were able to keep everything in front of them and ward off the early pressure.

Despite seeing much less possession in the first period (37 per cent), Howe’s team were extremely clinical with their chances, with two counter-attacks leading to close-range finishes for Isak and Gordon that gave Sa absolutely no chance.
Despite looking impressive on the ball, the visitors were unable to test Dubravka in the opening 45 minutes, with their few half-chances flying either wide or high of the crossbar.
Despite the need to pull two goals back, O’Neil doesn’t have many options to call upon from his bench - with the injury to Hwang severely limiting his attacking choices.

20-year old Chirewa could provide a pacey option on the wing in place of Bellegarde, while a change at wing-back and the introduction of Hugo Bueno could help the visitors get higher up the pitch as legs tire in the second half.

Newcastle will be looking to keep play in front of them and preserve the win and clean sheet, with the experience of Lascelles and the counter-attacking prowess of Almiron likely to be called upon by Howe after the restart.
Substitute goalkeeper Bentley is called upon to play in the second half, with Sa apparently unable to continue between the posts after half-time.
Neto does not return to the pitch after the interval either, with Fraser taking his place in attack.
Wolves get the match restarted from the kick-off!
The next goal will be key in this match, as it could either spark Wolves into a potential comeback, or seal the game for Newcastle, who would be three ahead.
Now without Neto either, it’s looking like a difficult task for the visitors to once again make it a contest; though it would be the perfect time for Fraser to find his first Premier League goal.
Worrying signs for Newcastle, as Trippier has immediately gone down after a tussle with Ait Nouri, signalling to the coach he is in need of treatment.
The medical staff has come onto the pitch to have a look at the captain, while Howe sparks his bench into life.
Trippier has limped off and remains deep in conversation with a member of the Newcastle medical staff.
It first appeared as though the England international would be able to retake his place, but that won’t be the case as Livramento comes on in his stead.
Play restarts through a Dubravka goal-kick, with Trippier heading directly into the tunnel towards the medical room at St.
James’ Park, and Burn the new Newcastle captain.
Sarabia is averaging a goal involvement every 122 minutes in the Premier League this season (three goals, six assists in 1096 minutes).
Of all players to play 500 or more minutes in a single campaign for Wolves, only Steven Fletcher has a better average across a campaign (one every 116 minutes in 2010-11).
OFF THE LINE! Gordon picks up possession inside the penalty area and spots the overlapping run of Burn, playing a lovely backheel layoff into the path of the right-back.
He chips a cross towards the penalty spot for the diving Willock, whose headed effort is cleared off the line by Toti!
Guimaraes’s outswinging corner finds the head of Burn, who fails to hit the target with his headed effort.
A change in defence for Wolves sees Toti make way after his key goal-line clearance.
Hugo Bueno is selected to replace him.
Semedo mistimes his step and brings Gordon down ahead of the technical areas.
It’s a free-kick for Newcastle near the halfway line, which they use to play backwards into defence.
Kilman sends a cross into the penalty area looking for the leap of Mario Lemina but it proves an easy catch for Dubravka, on the edge of his six-yard box.
Bellegarde leans back and curls a strike towards goal that fails to dip as it sails high above the crossbar.
The forward claims a corner-kick as he heads over towards the flag but the referee spots it correctly, pointing to the 18-yard box for a goal-kick.
Murphy stands a cross up towards the penalty spot that Kilman somehow manages to miss despite his leap, but Dawson is quick to follow up and volley the danger away despite the lurking Isak.
GREAT STOP! Bellegarde picks out a lovely cross to the far post for Sarabia, who meets it with a side-footed volley from an acute angle.
Already heading down to the turf, Dubravka somehow manages to keep himself upright and parry it behind!
Isak goes off having put his side ahead after just 14 minutes, with Barnes given a chance to stretch his legs.
Almiron has 20 minutes to impress as he takes over on the right wing for Murphy.
Willock is also recalled to the bench in a triple substitution for Newcastle.
Miley enters the fray.

Schar hoists a lovely ball over the top of the defence from inside his own half for Miley, who is beaten to the pass at the edge of the 18-yard box by Bentley, who came a long way off his line to make the grab.

DUBRAVKA TO THE RESCUE! Semedo curls an inch-perfect cross into the penalty area for Bellegarde, whose header towards the corner is pounced upon by the goalkeeper, who somehow manages to make a clean, two-handed grab and prevent a rebound!
Newcastle have conceded 23 goals in their last eight Premier League games, as many as they had in their previous 20.
Indeed, only Brentford (24) have shipped more goals than the Magpies in the competition since Christmas.
Guimaraes’ inswinging corner from the left finds Burn at the near post, whose flick-on causes a scramble inside the six-yard box.
Unable to turn it home, Dawson manages to eventually hit it clear and force Newcastle to come forward again from the back.
Quick thinking from Bentley prevents a third Newcastle goal, with Guimaraes’ pass over the top finding the run of Almiron.
After taking a touch to set himself, the substitute winger fails to get a shot away from an acute angle, with the goalkeeper immediately coming forward to close down the space.
20-year old Chirewa gets an appearance on the left wing, as Bellegarde is given an early rest.
Mario Lemina makes way with under 10 minutes to go, as O'Neil continues to roll the dice by sending on Traore.
Barnes looks to get forward down the left wing and challenge the defender, but thinking twice, the substitute turns around and plays a simple pass back down the wing for Miley.
With sights set on the three points and the clean sheet, it’s a prudent decision.
Ait Nouri is first called for a foul on Livramento on the touchline, before venting his frustration in the direction of the referee.
It’s a yellow card for the Wolves wing-back; the first booking of the match.
Sarabia’s volley across the face of goal is whacked away by Schar, but only as far as Kilman, 20 yards from goal.
The Wolves captain looks for the spectacular finish and strikes the ball with his left foot before it can bounce, but he sends his well-timed hit high and wide of the target.
Newcastle have lost just one of their eight Premier League home games against Wolves (four wins and three draws), a 1-2 defeat in December 2018 under Rafa Benitez.
The fourth official indicates five minutes will be added to the end of the match for stoppages.

LIVRAMENTO MAKES IT THREE! 3-0! A first Newcastle goal for the full-back adds the cherry on top of an otherwise perfect day, latching onto Schar’s long-range pass in acres of space on the wing before dribbling through the entire Wolves defence and somehow scuffing an unwitting shot past the oncoming Bentley!
Livramento still had a lot of work to do to find the back of the net, but Schar's phenomenal pass to find him in space is a worthy assist on Newcastle's third goal of the day.
Anderson gets two minutes to play in injury time, with Gordon not risked any further with the result secured.
FULL-TIME: NEWCASTLE 3-0 WOLVES.
Newcastle take all three points with a superb three-goal showing at St.
James’ Park, beating Wolves comprehensively 3-0.

Isak put the hosts ahead with an opportunistic header following Guimaraes’ blocked shot 14 minutes in, and Gordon would double their advantage 19 minutes later with a tap-in finish after Sa failed to claim the ball despite coming off his line.

Without many senior attacking options on the bench and forced into two changes at the half - including one to his goalkeeper - O’Neil was unable to change the game in the second half, which allowed the Magpies to grow in confidence and possession.

Howe’s side looked to control the remainder of the game and secure the clean sheet by forcing their opponents to chase, but Livramento’s incredible, mazey goal would add an unexpected third in injury time and seal the result.
A first Premier League defeat since February 10 sees Wolves drop into 10th place ahead of a meeting with Fulham next Sunday, while seventh-placed Newcastle travel to play Chelsea in nine days.
That concludes our commentary of the Premier League fixture between Newcastle United and Wolves- we hope you’ve enjoyed it!
